title: Defense in layers
question: How does the body stop germs that get past its first defenses?
hook: Your body has a quick general response and a slower learner, and the first sets off the second.
idea: Defenses come in layers of increasing specificity, and the adaptive layer remembers pathogens so it can answer faster next time.

beats.prompt: Put the layers of defense in the order a pathogen meets them.
items: The innate system gives an immediate, non-specific response
The adaptive system tailors its response during the infection
Immunological memory is kept after the pathogen is gone
beats.explain: Barriers come first, the innate response follows if they are breached, the adaptive system is activated by the innate response, and its memory is retained afterwards.

beats.prompt: Sort each description into the system it belongs to.
items: Gives a preconfigured response to broad groups of situations
Tailors a response to each stimulus
beats.explain: The innate system reacts broadly and at once, while the adaptive system tailors and remembers its response.

beats.prompt: A person fought off a virus last year and meets the same virus again today. Compared with the first time, what happens?

choices.label: The response is faster and stronger
The response is just as slow, because the body starts over
choices.feedback: It tempts because each infection feels new, but the improved response is retained after the pathogen is eliminated.

choices.label: The response is weaker, because the system is used up
choices.feedback: Nothing is used up; immunological memory is kept and the adaptive system mounts stronger attacks each time.

beats.explain: Immunological memory lets the adaptive system mount faster and stronger attacks each time it meets the pathogen.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which one?
steps: Adaptive immunity learns to recognize pathogens.
This creates an immunological memory, so later encounters bring a stronger response.
That memory is the fundamental basis of vaccination.
So the innate system, found in all animals, must be what remembers pathogens.
beats.explain: The innate response is preconfigured and non-specific; the memory comes from adaptive immunity.
